channel.title: Wire — Programming
channel.description: Programming from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: France to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls
item.description: After a joint call by 11 consumer groups, the French parliament approved a law to impose fines on individuals or companies that make unsolicited marketing calls, which can be reported through a public website. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: More than 10 firms pay up to $100k a month for access to Truth Social posts
item.description: Trump Media expects the controversial service, which launched this month, to provide a new revenue stream, as it posts a quarterly loss. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: The UK's War on Anonymity Has Come to America
item.description: The NGOs Behind Britain's Digital ID Laws are Targeting American Statehouses (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Illinois just passed a law that puts Linux on the hook for age verification
item.description: Illinois signed HB5511 on July 31. Past the TikTok and Instagram headlines is a mandate for operating systems, with no exemption for open source. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Stop Killing Games: It's time to sue Sony, join us
Reviewing code is a skill
item.description: A discussion on code review with short case studies and links to research on expertise. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Software Engineering Is Cool, But Is It Interesting?
Squeak 6.1
item.description: These release notes are optimized for viewing inside Squeak, as they contain a lot of interactive examples. On this page, interactive links open in SqueakJS, which is a browser-based Smalltalk VM with some limitations. (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: Making [etched] holograms with a pen plotter
There's a dungeon under this blog
item.description: A multiplayer dungeon crawler hidden in a static site: WebRTC with no server, a world derived from the date, and monsters run by whoever has the lowest peer id. (1 source: lobsters)
